request.what: Treasury withdrawal to fund Intersect Technical Steering Committee Support activities for 12 months across community engagement, protocol governance, and independent technical review.

claims.claim: Intersect requests $298,250, stated as 1,193,000 ADA, for 12 months of Technical Steering Committee support.
The budget is allocated as 256,000 ADA for WP1, 832,000 ADA for WP2, and 105,000 ADA for WP3, totaling 1,193,000 ADA.

WP1 funds expert attendance at major ecosystem events and commissioning technical reports on topics including throughput, finality, governance, quantum resistance, economic utility, and partner chains.
WP2 funds the Parameter Committee, CIP editors, and Hard Fork Working Group to support protocol settings advice, improvement pipeline maintenance, and safe protocol upgrade coordination.
WP3 funds a pilot independent technical review programme launching in 2027 with conflict-of-interest provisions, published recusals, and open reviewer selection against documented criteria.
The proposal states that technical workshops, the Security Council, and the Bug Bounty Programme are funded separately through the main Intersect budget and are not included in this request.

The proposal states that it achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase and provides references to voting documentation, final audited results, and an audit report.
The proposer states the requested amount does not breach the applicable 350M Net Change Limit for Epoch 613 to Epoch 713 at the moment of submission.

Independent audits and assurance for this proposal will be provided by Appold, with possible reviews including deliverable verification, control testing, spend validation, and milestone evidence assessment.

Intersect states it will administer the funds through Sundae Labs treasury management smart contracts with specified TRSC and PSSC addresses, multisignature-style permission thresholds, external oversight entities, and a public dashboard for auditing.

summary: The proposal asks for 1,193,000 ADA to fund 12 months of TSC support through three work packages covering technical coordination, protocol governance support, and a 2027 pilot technical review programme, with smart-contract-based fund administration and several external references for budget process and contract assurance.
